key_insight: Combining REM sleep behavior disorder or dream enactment behavior with reduced smell identified groups highly enriched for a Parkinson’s-associated biomarker before clinically significant motor symptoms.
clinical_relevance: These recruitment strategies could help assemble biologically defined early neuronal synucleinopathy cohorts for clinical trials.
method: Recruited participants with sleep-study-confirmed REM sleep behavior disorder or centrally identified reduced smell.
Stratified participants by reduced smell and self-reported dream enactment behavior.
Assessed clinical features, cerebrospinal fluid alpha-synuclein seed amplification and dopamine transporter imaging.
evidence_signal: Alpha-synuclein assay positivity was 94% for RBD with reduced smell, 85% for reduced smell with dream enactment, 40% for RBD without reduced smell and 55% for reduced smell without dream enactment.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish how reliably biomarker positivity predicts progression to clinically manifest Parkinson’s disease.
paper_title: Strategies to establish a biologically defined Parkinson's disease cohort prior to the onset of clinically significant motor symptoms
